root_cause: The drawer opens but focus remains on the triggering button because the dialog element is not focusable and no focus management is performed after showing it.
repair_strategy: In DialogBase._showElement, after showing the dialog (modal or non‑modal), set tabindex="-1" on the dialog and call focus() to move keyboard focus into the drawer, ensuring the first focusable element (the close button) can be reached with Tab.
expected_accessibility_effect: Focus will be moved into the drawer when opened, allowing sequential Tab navigation to reach the close button and other controls without a pointer.
functional_risks: Setting tabindex=-1 may interfere if the dialog already uses a custom tabindex for other purposes.
Non‑modal drawers with scroll behavior might receive unexpected focus, but the negative tabindex removes it from tab order.
If the dialog contains elements that expect initial focus elsewhere, this could override that intention.
verification_requirements: After pressing Enter on the filters button, focus must be on #filters-close.
Subsequent Tab presses must move focus to #in-stock, then #waterproof, then #apply.
Escape key must close the drawer and return focus to #filters-open.
Clicking Show results must update the applied output correctly.
Ensure the drawer still opens/closes correctly for mouse users.
